subject: general
question: Which of the following materials is used as a binding agent in organic brake linings?
solution:
The correct answer is __Resin.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Resin__ is widely used as a binding agent in organic brake linings.
 
• It provides the necessary cohesion to hold the brake lining materials together.
 
• Resin ensures durability and stability under high temperatures and pressure during braking.
 
• Its high binding strength prevents the brake lining from disintegrating under stress.
 
• Resins are typically combined with fillers and fibers to enhance performance and wear resistance.
 
• They also contribute to noise reduction and smoother braking operations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Rubber:**

 
 
• Rubber is used in brake linings primarily for flexibility and noise reduction but is not the primary binding agent.
 
 
 
• **Cotton:**
 
 
• Cotton fibers may be included as a filler material in some brake linings to improve heat resistance.
 
 
 
• **Metal Powder:**
 
 
• Metal powders are used to enhance thermal conductivity and strength but do not act as a binder.
